paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is not done with anyone. Paul asks if Israel stumbled so as to fall beyond recovery, and his answer is "Certainly not!" (Romans 11:11). If God can graft broken branches back in, then nobody who is still breathing is a lost cause. That includes the person you gave up on, and it includes you on your worst day.

Now hear the other half, because Paul won't let us skip it. If you're a grafted-in wild olive shoot, you don't hold up the root. "You do not support the root, but the root supports you" (Romans 11:18). So Paul says "do not boast" (Romans 11:18), and "Do not be arrogant, but be afraid" (Romans 11:20). You stand by faith, not by being better than anybody. I once sat in a drawer for years, so trust me, nobody in this bakery gets to strut.

So hold two things at once, baker. Paul tells us to notice God's "kindness and severity" (Romans 11:22), and the kindness is for you "if you continue in His kindness" (Romans 11:22). Stay close to the root, stay humble, and keep hoping for the ones who are far away. "God is able to graft them in again" (Romans 11:23).
